source_ref: Yang Q, Operario D, Zaller N, Huang W, Dong Y, Zhang H (2018) PLOS ONE 13(2):e0191632, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0191632 (CC BY 4.0); S1 Dataset SPSS .sav (journal.pone.0191632.s001, cached .cache/yang_2018_cesd/s001.sav) value labels for the response anchors and depressionS for the scoring check; item wording and instructions from the appendix of Front Psychol 2020 10.3389/fpsyg.2020.523950 (PMC7543651, CC BY) reproducing Radloff 1977 items 1-20; processing script data/yang_2018_cesd.py
note: data/yang_2018_cesd.py melts the PLOS S1 .sav columns E1..E20 straight through, so the IRW item code IS the source column name -- no positional inference on the code. But the .sav's variable labels for those twenty columns are bare placeholders ('01  e1' .. '20  e20'), so it carries no item wording, and the paper (Measures) only names the scale: 'Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D) [39]' with a cutoff of 16. mapping_basis=reconstructed: item_text is canonical Radloff (1977) CES-D wording aligned to the codes by assuming E<i> = CES-D item <i>, taken verbatim from the CC BY appendix of Front Psychol 2020 10.3389/fpsyg.2020.523950 (PMC7543651), the same source used for huang_2016_cesd and gan_2015_cesd; 'instructions' is that appendix's CES-D instruction text. option_text is the study's own: the S1 .sav's value-label set attached to E1, verbatim including its spacing ('Never/ rarely(during the past week, it happened less than a day)'), transcribed unchanged onto resp 1-4; E5/E10/E15/E20 carry an abbreviated copy of the same four anchors ('Never/ rarely','Seldom','Often','Almost always') and E2-E4 etc carry none, so the full-form set was shipped for all twenty items. Storage direction checked, not assumed: the live table stores RAW 1-4 responses -- recoding to 0-3 and reversing E4/E8/E12/E16 reproduces the .sav's own depressionS ('total score of CES-D') for 358/358 respondents and the paper's published M=12.9 SD=9.0 range 0-46 (observed 12.877/8.979/0-46), while no reversal matches only 36/358 -- so every item's anchors ship ascending. Administered in Chinese (Hefei, Anhui); no Chinese wording exists anywhere in the deposit (the S1 .sav's only CJK content is one unrelated 0/1 value-label pair) or in the paper's supplements, so English sits in the base fields as the documented fallback with language=Chinese and no _translated columns. translation_source=mixed: item_text and instructions are the canonical instrument's published English (third-party CC BY reproduction of Radloff 1977), option_text is the authors' own English in their deposited .sav. Rights: no restriction locatable or quotable for the CES-D, which has no row in instrument_rights_register.csv and already ships in the corpus for conner_2017_cesd, dwyer_2019_clinton_cesd, gan_2015_cesd, huang_2016_cesd and quinn_2023_roommate_cesd; deposit is CC BY 4.0. Step 3b: checked that E1-E20 is the depression scale and not the companion 20-item anxiety scale in the same file (E21-E40, summed into 'anxietyS') -- the .sav labels depressionS 'total score of CES-D' and it reconstructs from E1-E20 exactly.
public_note: The Yang et al. respondents answered a Chinese CES-D, but no Chinese wording appears in the deposited SPSS file or the paper's supplements, so the item text shipped here is the canonical English Radloff (1977) CES-D and the response anchors are the authors' own English labels from that file; the items are stored raw (resp 1 = least frequent) for all twenty, including the four positively worded ones (E4, E8, E12, E16), which the authors reverse before summing.

source_ref: Yang W, Zhang J, Yang X, Zhang Y (2023) 'The influence of the brand image of green agriculture products on China's consumption intention--The mediating role of perceived value', PLOS ONE 18(10):e0292633, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0292633, CC BY 4.0. ITEM WORDING: Table 1 'Measurement scales for each variable', which is published as an IMAGE only (no text/HTML endpoint; grep for 'F1' over the scraped article returns 0 hits) -- fetched as https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/figure/image?size=large&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0292633.t001, sha256 1634e3407958acb0b96331fa1fea7af9e53557e5a57e9c8a0b1e19c6e1794b7c. CONSTRUCT ASSIGNMENT cross-check: Table 3 (t003 image, sha256 2c1d089d71d448a3f1badd8d0d6fbe3b345ad898c7cdb1b8bade23856909b18b), which repeats the code->latent-variable assignment with Cronbach's alpha per construct. RAW DATA: S1 File CSV (.s001), sha256 5aabb592951f0b0bff81eab1baeb0203fce733c461bdf8f04a495758eea4504e, header 'NO.,Gender,Age,Education background,Monthly income,A1..F4' -- codes only, no wording, pure ASCII (no CJK anywhere). IRW script: data/yang_2023_green_brand.py. All fetched 2026-09-16, cached under itemtext/.cache/yang_2023_consumption_intent/.
note: PASS WITH A TABLE-NAME CAVEAT. 20 rows = 4 items x resp 1..5; validate_items.R --table-sets passes both sets exactly. (1) STEP 3b INSTRUMENT MISMATCH, and it is the main finding: this table is NOT consumption intention. data/yang_2023_green_brand.py assigns columns F1-F4 to 'yang_2023_consumption_intent' and E1-E3 to 'yang_2023_perceived_value', but the paper's Table 1 and Table 3 both assign F1-F4 to CUSTOMER PERCEIVED VALUE (Xie Qiang / Sweeney sources) and E1-E3 to CONSUMPTION INTENTION (Chan R.Y.K / Rauchov / Zeithaml sources). The two IRW table names are swapped. Confirmed against the data rather than taken from the paper: recomputing Cronbach's alpha per letter block on the S1 File reproduces all six of Table 3's published alphas to 3dp (A .807/.807, B .779/.779, C .712/.712, D .743/.743, F .849/.849, E .934/.934; largest deviation .0005), so the F block IS the .849 'Customer perceived value' factor and misses the .934 'Consumption intention' factor by .085. Per the Step 3b rule the extraction follows the live data: item_text is the perceived-value wording and the `instrument` field names Customer perceived value. The table NAME and its dictionary Description should be corrected (swap with yang_2023_perceived_value) -- logged in notes_yang_2023_consumption_intent.csv. The sibling table yang_2023_perceived_value is NOT in this round's scope and was not touched. (2) CODE DERIVATION: the code IS the source column name. The script's SCALES dict lists the literal strings 'F1'..'F4' and melts with var_name='item'; no positional step, no rename. (3) mapping_basis=paper_explicit, not data_labels: the S1 header carries bare codes and no text at any level (it is a plain CSV, no variable or value labels exist), so the words come from Table 1, which prints each item beside the very code the data uses. Verification is PARTIAL rather than VERIFIED -- see verify_yang_2023_consumption_intent.R. (4) LANGUAGE / FALLBACK: administered in Chinese (341 consumers of green agricultural products recruited across 32 Chinese provincial capitals, Nov 2022-Jan 2023). No Chinese wording exists in scope: the article has exactly ONE supplementary file, the S1 CSV, and it is pure ASCII with zero CJK characters; there is no questionnaire supplement. So the 2026-09-01 fallback applies -- the study's own English from Table 1 goes in the base fields, the four _translated columns are empty, language=Chinese, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. (5) OCR CAVEAT: Table 1 is an image, so item_text is a transcription from the PNG and is worth a human spot-check. Transcribed character by character, including the source's own inconsistent terminal punctuation elsewhere in the table; all four F items end in '?' in the original. (6) OPTION TEXT: only the two endpoints are labelled anywhere in the paper -- 'The questionnaires ... scored on a 5-point Likert scale ... That is, 1 means "disagree," and 5 means "agree".' So resp 1='disagree', resp 5='agree' and resp 2/3/4 are left BLANK rather than padded with their own numbers. These anchors are the paper's English methods-section gloss of the administered Chinese anchors, not a printed response scale. (7) instructions and section_prompt are blank: the paper describes the administration but never quotes an instruction stem addressed to respondents, and none was invented. section_id is the trivial yang_2023_consumption_intent_1; correct_response blank throughout (attitude scale, no key). (8) RIGHTS: no block. The items are the study's own composite, not verbatim PERVAL or any other named publisher instrument, and they are printed in full in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article ('This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License, which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium'). No fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause could be located or quoted for this wording, and the instrument has no row in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. Shipped under 'silence is permission'; per the standing rule a round may not write a ship row, so no register row was added. (9) UNRELATED SOURCE DEFECT, recorded so nobody re-derives it: the paper's Table 1 prints the third social-image item as C3 while the raw file's column is C4 (the alpha match above uses C1,C2,C4 and reproduces .712 exactly), and Table 4's descriptive rows are shifted relative to their construct labels (its row 1 'Agribusiness image' 3.9/0.90 matches the F block's 3.987/0.907, its row 5 'Perceived value' 4.1/0.79 matches the D block's 4.194/0.794). Table 4 was therefore NOT used as evidence; Tables 1 and 3 agree with each other and with the data.
public_note: This table is misnamed: its items F1-F4 are the study's CUSTOMER PERCEIVED VALUE scale, not consumption intention -- the paper's Tables 1 and 3 assign F1-F4 to perceived value and E1-E3 to consumption intention, and recomputing Cronbach's alpha per block from the study's own S1 File reproduces all six published alphas to three decimals (this block .849, matching 'Customer perceived value'; the consumption-intention alpha is .934, which this block misses by .085). The consumption-intention items are in the sibling table yang_2023_perceived_value. The item wording shown is also English: the survey was administered in Chinese and no Chinese wording is published in the article's single supplementary file, so the authors' own English from Table 1 is what ships, transcribed from a table published only as an image.
